titleStmt.title: History of the Zhou Dynasty · Western Zhou 西周

div.interp: 公将不利于孺子: the Metal-bound Coffer of the Documents, after Legge, "the duke would do no good to the (king's) young son".
匽: the form of 燕, Yan, in the bronze inscriptions.
顽民: Legge's rendering in the Charge to the Duke of Bi of the Documents, 毖殷顽民，迁于洛邑, "Cautiously did he deal with the refractory people of Yin, and removed them to the city of Lo".
昜: so written in a bronze inscription of the early Western Zhou, 王命昜伯侯于晋，唯王廿又八祀; the transmitted texts have Tang 唐.
刑错: 错 is read as 措, to lay aside (Ying Shao, in the Jijie).
荆: Jing, the name by which the inscriptions and the old texts call Chu.
过伯簋: translated with Robert Eno's version at hand (Inscriptional Records of the Western Zhou, no. 39), which has "Elder of Guo" and "clan shrine". 白 and 乍 are the inscription's forms of 伯 and 作.
丧六师于汉: after Legge's translation of the Bamboo Annals, "The king's six armies perished in the Han".
班簋: translated after Robert Eno (Inscriptional Records of the Western Zhou, no. 46), who has "bring peace to the eastern lands" and "none do not submit".
密: the state of Mi, traditionally placed at Lingtai, Gansu, on the land of the former Mixu.
